subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should OpenClaw collect inbound WhatsApp call activity at all, and if so which call statuses may be retained or exposed to agents after the WhatsApp access-control boundary?
rationale: The choice creates a new privacy-sensitive activity surface and determines the meaning of relationship/contact state; source inspection cannot safely choose consent, retention, or agent-exposure policy.

options.title: Approve opt-in normalized activity
options.body: Add a WhatsApp-plugin-owned opt-in that exposes only documented, access-filtered call activity needed for contact-state workflows.

options.title: Keep calls out of agent state
options.body: Leave Baileys call events unconsumed and direct relationship tracking to messages or an external integration.

options.title: Design a generic activity API first
options.body: Define a cross-channel, privacy-reviewed activity contract before adding any WhatsApp-specific call event exposure.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in normalized activity
recommendation.body: Add a WhatsApp-plugin-owned opt-in that exposes only documented, access-filtered call activity needed for contact-state workflows.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the strongest recent history on the WhatsApp runtime boundary and previously scoped the request as WhatsApp-plugin-owned.
